Peer feedback for appraisals at consulting firms

Built from everyone on the project, not one manager's memory.

For firms of 40 to 400 people in India. Every two weeks, the people on each project give two minutes of feedback. Partners and engagement managers see it before calibration.

12-week pilot for up to 40 people, ₹25,000 plus GST, credited to your first annual bill.

See the 2-minute walkthrough

What happens at calibration today: last-project bias

The rating reflects the last project, usually its final weeks, because that is the one the rating manager saw.

Staffing
At calibration, the partner a consultant is staffed with now carries the most weight.
Recency
Recent projects count for more than the ones before them.
Rolled off
A consultant who rolled off a project months ago has nobody to present the case.
Chasing forms
HR is still chasing feedback forms in the week the ratings close.
Attrition
A strong consultant misses a designation and leaves after the hike letters go out.

Two minutes every two weeks

The project team gives feedback while the work is fresh

Every two weeks, Fortnightly Feedback asks each person about the people they worked with on the project: how it went, and which of the firm's values stood out. It takes about two minutes.

The head of talent sets it up

With the Admin role, the head of talent sets the firm's values and the two-week cycle, and adds people from a spreadsheet. Sphyr does not replace your HRMS: it runs alongside the one you already use (Keka, Zoho), with no integration to set up.

Each consultant sees how their work is landing

Insights shows a consultant's score cycle by cycle and the comments colleagues wrote, without the writer's name.

Partners and engagement managers see the whole project team

Partners and engagement managers who have the Manager role see Team Insights: how the project team is rated, and the edit requests waiting for them. The ratings at calibration stay with the partners.

Who gets a say

Each consultant adds the colleagues they work with closely on the project: the engagement manager, seniors, peers and juniors.

From the second cycle, a consultant can also invite a client lead by email, with the partner's agreement.

What you get and what stays private

Setup and training
Our team sets Sphyr up with your head of talent and trains your people, with training materials they keep. Support is part of the price.
What stays private
Ratings are grouped before anyone sees them, and the person rated sees comments without the writer's name. Managers approve requests to edit sent feedback, so they see who asked. On a project of three or four people, a comment can be easy to attribute even without a name. Sphyr has no minimum number of responses before comments are shown, so small teams should expect grouped ratings, not anonymous comments.
Your results
Results stay with your firm unless you agree to share them.
What a pilot measures
Participation in each cycle and how many colleagues give feedback to each consultant. At the end, whether partners saw something new before calibration, and whether consultants want to keep going.

Price and pilot

Start with a pilot
₹25,000one time, plus GST

12 weeks, six cycles, up to 40 people

The ₹25,000 comes off your first annual bill if you sign.

If you do not sign, we delete your ratings and comments. The fee is not returned.

The plan
₹149per employee per month, billed yearly, plus GST

Same rate for every employee and firm size.

New joiners are billed from the month they join. Clients you invite give feedback free.

A 150-person firm pays ₹22,350 a month, plus GST: about ₹2.7 lakh a year. By our own estimate, replacing one consultant costs a firm about ₹5 lakh to ₹8.6 lakh (recruiter fee, the empty seat and ramp-up time).
